checks.english: 1 And when Tiberius Caesar, the emperor of the Romans, was laboring under a grievous disease, and understanding that there was at Jerusalem a certain Physician, Jesus by Name, who by a single word cured all sicknesses, he, not knowing that the Jews and Pilate had put Him to death, ordered a certain friend of his named Volusianus: 2 “Go as quickly as possible across the seas; and you will tell Pilate, my servant and friend, to send me this Physician, so that He may restore me to my former health.” 3 And this Volusianus, having heard the emperor’s command, immediately departed and came to Pilate as he had been commanded. 4 And he related to the same Pilate what had been entrusted to him by Tiberius Caesar, saying, “Tiberius Caesar, the emperor of the Romans, your master, having heard that in this city there is a Physician who by His word alone heals sicknesses, begs you earnestly to send Him to him for the curing of his sickness.” 5 Pilate, hearing this, was very greatly afraid, knowing that through envy he had caused Him to be put to death. 6 Pilate answered the same messenger thus, saying, “This Man was a criminal, and a Man who drew to Himself all the people; so a council of the wise men of the city was held, and I caused Him to be crucified.” 7 And this messenger returning to his inn, met a certain woman named Veronica, who had been a friend of Jesus; and he said: “O woman, a certain Physician who was in this city, who cured the sick by a word alone, why have the Jews put Him to death?” 8 And she began to weep, saying, “Oh my lord, my God and my Lord, whom Pilate for envy delivered, condemned, and ordered to be crucified.” 9 Then he, being exceedingly grieved, said: “I am vehemently grieved that I am unable to accomplish that for which my lord had sent me.” 10 And Veronica said to him: “When my Lord was going around preaching, and I, much against my will, was deprived of His presence, I wished [for] His picture to be painted for me, in order that, while I was deprived of His presence, the figure of His picture might at least provide me consolation. 11 And when I was carrying the canvas to the painter to be painted, my Lord met me and asked where I was going. 12 And when I had disclosed to Him the cause of my journey, He asked for the cloth from me and gave it back to me impressed with the image of His noble face. 13 Therefore, if your lord will devoutly gaze on His face, he will immediately obtain the benefit of health.” 14 And he said to her: “Is a picture of such a sort obtainable by gold or silver?” 15 She said to him: “No; but by the pious influence of devotion. I will therefore set out with you, and carry the picture to be seen by Caesar, and come back again.” 16 Therefore, Volusianus came with Veronica to Rome and said to Tiberius the emperor: “Jesus, whom you have been longing for, Pilate and the Jews have delivered to an unjust death, and have through envy affixed to the scaffold of the cross. 17 There has therefore come with me a certain matron, bringing a picture of Jesus Himself; and if you will devoutly look on it, you will immediately obtain the benefit of your health.” 18 Caesar therefore ordered the way to be strewn with silk cloths, and the picture to be presented to him; and as soon as he had looked on it, he regained his former health. 19 Pontius Pilate, therefore, by the command of Caesar, is taken and brought through to Rome. 20 Caesar, hearing that Pilate had arrived at Rome, was filled with exceeding fury against him and caused him to be brought to him. 21 But Pilate brought down with him the seamless tunic of Jesus; and he wore it on him in the presence of the emperor. 22 And as soon as the emperor saw him, he laid aside all his anger, and immediately rose up to meet him. Nor was he able to speak harshly to him in anything; and he who seemed so terrible and fierce in his absence, now in his presence is somehow found to be mild. 23 And when he had sent him away, he immediately blazed out against him terribly, crying out that he was a wretch, inasmuch as he had not at all shown him the fury of his heart. 24 And he immediately made him be called back, swearing and declaring that he was the son of death, and that it was infamous that he should live on the earth. 25 And as soon as he saw him, he immediately saluted him and threw away all the ferocity of his mind. 26 Everyone marveled; and he himself wondered why he should thus blaze out against Pilate when he was absent, and that while he was present he could say nothing to him sternly. 27 Then, by a divine impulse, or perhaps by the advice of some Christian, he caused him to be stripped of that tunic, and immediately resumed his former ferocity of mind against him. 28 And when at this the emperor wondered very greatly, it was told to him that that tunic had belonged to the Lord Jesus. 29 Then the emperor ordered him to be kept in prison, until he should deliberate in a council of the wise men what ought to be done with him. 30 And a few days later, sentence was therefore passed on Pilate, that he should be condemned to the most disgraceful death. Pilate, hearing this, killed himself with his own knife, and by such a death ended his life. 31 When Caesar knew of the death of Pilate, he said: “Truly he has died by a most disgraceful death, whom his own hand has not spared.” 32 He is therefore bound to a great mass and sunk into the Tiber River. But malignant and filthy spirits in his malignant and filthy body, all rejoicing together, kept moving themselves in the waters, and in a terrible manner brought lightnings and tempests, thunders and hailstorms, in the air, so that all men were kept in horrible fear. 33 Therefore, the Romans, drawing him out of the Tiber River, carried him down to Vienna in derision and sunk him in the Rhone River. For Vienna is called, as it were, Via Gehennae, “The Way of Gehenna,” because it was then a place of cursing. 34 But evil spirits were present there, working the same things in the same place. Those men therefore, not enduring such a visitation of demons, removed from themselves that vessel of blight and sent him to be buried in the territory of Losania. 35 And they, seeing that they were troubled by the aforementioned visitations, removed him from themselves and sunk him in a certain pit surrounded by mountains, where to this day, according to the account of some, certain diabolical machinations are said to bubble up.
checks.head: 1 罗马皇帝凯撒提庇留患了重病，听说耶路撒冷有一位名叫耶稣的医生，只需一句话，就能医好一切疾病。他不知道犹太人和彼拉多已经将祂杀害，便吩咐一位名叫沃卢西安的朋友说：2 “你要尽快渡海前去，告诉我的臣仆和朋友彼拉多，将这位医生送到我这里，使我恢复从前的健康。”3 沃卢西安听了皇帝的命令，就立刻启程，奉命来到彼拉多那里。4 他将凯撒提庇留所托付的话告诉彼拉多，说：“你的主、罗马皇帝凯撒提庇留，听说这城里有一位医生，单凭祂的话就能医治疾病。他恳切请求你将这人送到他那里，医治他的病。”5 彼拉多听了，极其惧怕，因为知道自己曾因嫉妒，下令将祂处死。6 彼拉多便这样回答那使者，说：“这人是个罪犯，招引所有百姓跟从祂；因此，城中的智慧人召开会议，我就命人将祂钉在十字架上。”7 使者回到客店，遇见一个名叫维罗尼卡的妇人，她从前是耶稣的朋友。他问她：“妇人，这城里曾有一位医生，只用一句话就医好病人，犹太人为什么将祂杀害呢？”8 她就哭起来，说：“哦，先生！那是我的神、我的主；彼拉多因嫉妒，将祂交出去，定了祂的罪，命人将祂钉在十字架上。”9 使者极其忧伤，说：“我不能办成主人差我来办的事，心里实在悲痛。”10 维罗尼卡对他说：“我的主四处传道的时候，我虽然极不情愿，却不能常在祂身边。我便盼望有人为我画一幅祂的像，好让我不能见祂的时候，至少能从画像中得些安慰。11 我拿着画布，要去找画师画像，路上遇见我的主；祂问我要往哪里去。12 我告诉祂出门的缘故，祂就向我要那块布，交还给我的时候，上面已经印着祂尊贵面容的形像。13 所以，你的主人若虔诚地瞻望祂的面容，就必立刻蒙恩，恢复健康。”14 使者问她：“这样的画像，可以用金银买到吗？”15 她对他说：“不能，惟有凭敬虔的诚心。因此，我愿与你一同起行，带着画像给凯撒看，然后再回来。”16 沃卢西安便与维罗尼卡来到罗马，对皇帝提庇留说：“你所切望见到的耶稣，已经被彼拉多和犹太人不义地处死；他们因嫉妒，将祂钉在十字架的木架上。17 不过，有一位妇人同我来了，带着耶稣本人的画像；你若虔诚地观看，就必立刻蒙恩，恢复健康。”18 凯撒便吩咐用丝绸铺路，将画像呈到自己面前。他一看见画像，就恢复了从前的健康。19 于是，本丢·彼拉多奉凯撒之命，被捕押送到罗马。20 凯撒听说彼拉多已到罗马，就向他大发烈怒，命人将他带来。21 彼拉多却将耶稣那件无缝的里衣一同带来，穿在身上，觐见皇帝。22 皇帝一看见他，就消了所有怒气，立刻起身迎接，竟无法对他说一句严厉的话。彼拉多不在场时，皇帝显得那么可怕、暴烈，如今到了他面前，却不知怎的温和起来。23 皇帝打发他离开以后，立刻又向他大发雷霆，高喊自己真是个无用的人，竟完全没有向他发出心中的怒气。24 他随即命人将彼拉多召回，起誓宣告他是该死的人，容他活在世上是一种耻辱。25 但皇帝一见到他，就立刻向他问安，心里所有的凶怒也都消散了。26 众人都很惊奇；连他自己也不明白，为什么彼拉多不在时，他就如此发怒；而彼拉多在场时，却说不出一句严厉的话。27 后来，或因神的感动，或因某个基督徒的建议，他命人脱去彼拉多那件里衣，心里对他的凶怒便立刻恢复如前。28 皇帝对此极其惊奇，有人就告诉他，那件里衣原属于主耶稣。29 皇帝于是命人将彼拉多关在监里，等候他召集智慧人商议，应当怎样处置。30 过了几天，就判彼拉多处以最羞辱的死刑。彼拉多听见，就用自己的刀自杀，以这样的死法结束了一生。31 凯撒得知彼拉多的死讯，说：“他连自己的手都不肯放过自己，确实死得极其羞辱。”32 于是，人将他绑在重物上，沉入台伯河。然而，那些住在他邪恶污秽身体里的邪恶污灵，都一同欢腾，在水中不断翻腾，又在空中兴起可怕的闪电、暴风、雷鸣和冰雹，使众人惊恐不已。33 罗马人便将他从台伯河中捞起，为羞辱他，将他运到维埃纳，沉入罗讷河。维埃纳仿佛就是“维亚·革亨那”，意为“地狱之路”，因为那时那里是受咒诅之地。34 但邪灵在那里，仍旧作同样的事。当地人受不了鬼魔如此侵扰，就将这带来灾害的器皿移走，送到洛萨尼亚境内埋葬。35 那里的人发现，上述灾害又临到自己，就将他迁走，沉入一个群山环绕的深坑。据一些人的说法，直到今日，那里仍有某些魔鬼作祟的迹象不断涌现。

checks.english: 34. Then they put in many beasts, while she stood, and stretched out her hands, and prayed. And when she had ended her prayer, she turned and saw a great tank full of water and said: “Now is it time that I should wash myself.” And she cast herself in, saying, “In the Name of Jesus Christ do I immerse myself on the last day.” And all the women saw it, and all the people wept, saying, “Do not cast yourself into the water,” so that even the governor wept that such great beauty should be devoured by seals. So, then, she cast herself into the water in the Name of Jesus Christ; and the seals, seeing the light of a flash of fire, floated dead on the top of the water. And there was around her a cloud of fire, so that neither did the beasts touch her, nor was she seen to be naked.
checks.head: 34. 他们又放进许多野兽，特格拉却站着，伸手祷告。祷告完毕，她转身看见一座盛满水的大池，就说：“现在是我当洗净自己的时候了。”她便跳进去，说：“在这末后的日子，我奉耶稣基督的名给自己施洗。”所有妇女都看见，众人哭着喊：“不要跳进水里！”连省长也哭了，因这样美丽的人竟要被海豹吞吃。她就这样奉耶稣基督的名跳进水里；海豹看见火焰闪光，都死了，浮在水面。她周围有火云环绕，使野兽不能碰她，也使人看不见她赤身。
